pinev: Five Mile Hill crest, named in the 1900 Tribune; Baty's 90-ft shaft was sunk from the crest. Crest is the highest point of the dune mass south of the harbour on 2016 Michigan 1 m lidar (237.7 m).
'Just back of the summit' (Grand Rapids Herald 1900), i.e. the landward (east) side of the crest, within the 250 m ring.

Five Mile Hill named as the dune on the state park's east boundary (WPA 1941); name still in use 1934. On lidar the mass has two knobs: 226 m at 43.0561,-86.2413 right above the park and the 237.7 m summit 320 m east, joined by a saddle near 205 m; the 400 m ring covers both.

The Grand Haven city water storage tanks stood on Five Mile Hill (Muskegon Chronicle 1932). On 2016 lidar a round levelled pad about 32 m across sits on the summit at 232 m (43.0564,-86.2371) with a second small pad just S and an access road winding up: the tank site. Pin moved onto it (about 55 m from the old crest pin); the 400 m ring is kept so the W knob stays inside.
The tank pad is in the NW¼ of sec 29 T8N R16W (BLM PLSS), where the 1912 Ottawa plat shows a 'City of Grand Haven' strip just S of the channel: city water-works ground.
Sanborn: two concrete reservoirs built 1912, 200 ft above the water works; the 1932 Chronicle only named them.

pinev: 1873 plat: N. A. Burton 160 = NW¼ sec 27 T2S R7W; Newbre farms across the S-line road; letter's paces put the well within ~120 m of the W quarter corner beside the 27/28 road.
W quarter corner from BLM PLSS (42.26852,-85.12030); the 27/28 road still shows on 2017 Michigan 1 m lidar; dry farmland.

The 1873 plat shows the graveyard at the SW corner of sec 27, matching the letter's graveyard reference; the well lies between it and the W quarter corner along the 27/28 road, nearer the quarter corner by the paces.

Free Press 15 Sep 1874: the well was about 5 mi SE of Battle Creek and about a mile from the Kalamazoo River, in N. A. Burton's pasture lot; the reporter paced from 'the half-mile stake' and found the distances exactly as the letter gave, which fits the W quarter corner of sec 27.

1894 Calhoun plat: no Burton or McArdill by then; at the W quarter of sec 27, E. Sanford 80, J. G. Ulrich 78 and H. C. Webster 39 N of the CJ&M railroad and an unlabelled 79 S of it; Newbre still in secs 34-35.

src: Atlas of Calhoun County (1894), Emmett Twp (PC (b) read)

tw-wi-milwaukee-schuerman-bottles.st: A Norwegian-language wire (Fergus Falls Ugeblad, 14 Aug 1902) says reporters found a wax-sealed jar with about $40 in silver and a 'key' (an 1876 date table), after eleven earlier bottles; it says the lot was bought for $10,000 from the estate of a Dr Casper Schuerman (the card's other sources say Joseph) and that $10,000 or more was believed buried.
